title: Cardinal Billing Account Autopay Draft, Retry and Fallback Schedule
content:
Automatic payments on a Cardinal Billing Account are drafted, re-presented after a failure and, after repeated failures, removed according to the pay plan.

| Pay plan | Draft offset (days before due date) | Retry after a failed draft (calendar days) | Number of re-presentments | Failed drafts before autopay is removed | Plan the account moves to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan | 0 | 0 (no retry) | 0 | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Cardinal Card Autopay Monthly Plan | 0 | 3 | 1 | 2 | Rank 1, the Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan |
| Cardinal EFT Autopay Monthly Plan | 0 | 3 | 1 | 2 | Rank 1, the Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan |
| Cardinal Three-Pay Plan | 0 | 0 (no retry) | 0 | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Cardinal Two-Pay Plan | 0 | 0 (no retry) | 0 | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Cardinal Paid-in-Full Plan | 0 | 0 (no retry) | 0 | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |

## Notes to the schedule

- A draft offset of 0 means the automatic payment is drafted on the due date itself; every plan drafts on the due date.
- The retry figure is the number of calendar days after a failed draft on which the draft is presented once more; 0 means there is no retry.
- Failed drafts are counted over the returned-payment lookback of the plan. On the two autopay plans, when failed drafts in that lookback reach 2, autopay is removed and the account moves to the plan of rank 1, the Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan.
- The plans without required autopay carry 0 in every column: no retry and no fallback move apply to them.

Hypothetical reading: on the Cardinal EFT Autopay Monthly Plan a draft that fails on its due date is presented once more 3 calendar days later.
